column2: The Shri seed, "apa" the power; the limbs by the seed itself. The word "Trailokyamohana" ending in "namah" is declared the mantra.
Its sage is Brahma, its metre Gayatri, its deity Shridhara; the Shri seed, "apa" the power; the six limbs by the seed itself.
Meditation, worship and so on are as told for Purushottama; a hundred thousand chants, and the offering only with ghee, a tenth part.
He should perform worship and offering with fragrant white flowers. When this is done, O best of Brahmins, Shridhara himself appears.
Achyuta-Ananta-Govinda in the dative ending with "namah": its sage is Shaunaka, the metre declared Virat.
The sages of these are held to be Parashara, Vyasa and Narada; the metre is Virat; the deity is Hari whose nature is the Supreme Brahman.
Its seed and power are the same as stated before by the practitioners. The god bearing conch and discus, four-armed, crowned,
with all weapons, standing above Garuda, worshipped by Sanaka and the other lords of sages and all the gods,
with Shri and Bhumi, bright as the rising sun, his earrings like the disc of the morning thousand-rayed sun,
for the protection of all the world, the endless, the god joyfully granting protection and boons always.
Having meditated thus, he should worship on the Vaishnava seat attentively; the first enclosure is with the discus, conch, mace and sword,
the second is told with pestle, bow, noose and goad; with Sanaka and others, Shakteya, Vyasa, Narada, Shaunaka,
the third is with the guardians of the world; the fourth is told. A hundred thousand chants, offering a tenth part with ghee is held.
When the mantra is perfected the mantra-knower should perform applications also: at the foot of a Shri-tree meditating on the Lord of gods, remembering the sick,
touching, chanting ten thousand or remembering the one to be cured in mind, O Brahmin, the mantra-knower frees the sick from disease within a circle.
One wishing for a bride should offer parched grain; for wealth, bilva; one wishing for clothes, perfumes and flowers; for health, sesame.
One who on Sunday stands in water up to the navel and chants a thousand and eight times surely destroys fever.
For marriage, chanting for a month while meditating on Krishna in the middle of the Moon's disc, a man would gain the desired bride, O Narada.
Having said "Vasudeva", then "nigadacheda" (cutter of fetters), "Vasudevaya", armour, weapon, ending in "svaha": this mantra is declared.
Narada is its sage, Gayatri its metre, Krishna its deity; "varma" the seed, "shira" the power; all else as with the ten-syllable.
Bala, with wind and long vowels..., "Jhintisha", "Atri", "Vyasaya", the heart: may the eight-syllable mantra protect.
Its sage Brahma; the metre Anushtubh; the deity Vyasa, son of Satyavati; the first the seed; "namah" the power; the limbs with long vowels and so on.

I remember for success Vyasa, son of Parashara, of most meritorious conduct: his hand shining with the explaining-mudra, seated on the seat of perfect yoga, holding his other hand on his left knee, treasury of fine knowledge, surrounded by hosts of Brahmins, calm-minded, with a body bright as a lotus.
He should chant eight thousand, perform gold-offerings with milk-rice, and on the seat stated before worship first the limbs of Vyasa.
In the east and the other directions he should worship Paila, Vaishampayana, Jaimini, Sumantu in the corners, Shri Shuka, Romaharshana,
Ugrashravas and the other sages, with Indra and the others with their weapons. The mantra-knower with perfected mantra thus
gains poetic power, fair offspring, power of exposition, fame and a heap of prosperity. Narasimha, Madhava, Lohita, "nigamadima"...
with "krishanu-jaya": a five-syllable mantra, the best remover of poison. Ananta, Pankti, Pakshindra, Muni: the metres and gods are held.
Om, Agnipriya as seed and power of the mantra are declared. "Jvala jvala mahamantrin svaha" is declared the heart.
At the end of the word "Garuda", "Chudanana-Shuchipriya": the head mantra from Garuda; "shikhe svaha" is the tuft mantra.
Having said the word "Garuda", he should say "prabhanjaya" twice, afterward "prabhedaya" twice, "vitrasaya vimardaya",
each twice, then "svaha": the armour mantra is held. After "ugrarupadhara", "sarvavishahara",
bhishaya twice, "sarvam daha daha", "bhasmikuru", then "svaha": this is declared the eye mantra.
After "apratihata-varna", "balaya prahata", and at the end "shasana", "hum phat svaha" is declared the weapon mantra.
He should place the letters on the feet, waist, heart, face and head.

I worship the glorious Lord of birds, bright as heated gold, his limbs adorned with hosts of serpent-kings, quieting at once the fierce poison of all who are bitten, bearing in his hands the boon and the fear-giving trembling snakes in his beak's tip, singing stainless Sama with his wings.
He should chant the mantra five hundred thousand and offer a tenth with sesame; he should worship Garuda, whose form is the Veda, on the alphabet seat.
Pakshirajaya svaha in the dative is remembered as the seat mantra. Having seen the limb, he should worship the nagas in the pericarp and yantras,
outside them the guardians of the world with their shining weapons. The mantra-knower so perfected destroys the two kinds of poison, and at death obtains the supreme abode of Shri Vishnu.
Now I shall tell the means of the inner dharma.
Having received the mantra, devoted to the teacher, reflecting in mind on all he wishes, established in his own dharma, he should please the teacher, meditating on his grace in himself.
He should learn from the good the dharmas that remove the fears of the surrendered, free of worldly and other-worldly worries, giving success.
He should always please the Vaishnavas, thinking of them as his chosen deity; he should never think of rebuking them or the like.
By the force of former karma whatever is to be in this life and enjoyed, and long life, Krishna himself will provide.
He should constantly meditate in his mind on Shri Krishna in eternal play; he should always serve Krishna in the glorious image-form.
He is to be thought of with undivided thought by the surrendered and seekers of refuge; the wise should stay indifferent to body and home.
Disrespect to the teacher, slander of the good, distinguishing Hari from Hari, slander of the Veda, committing sin on the strength of Hari's name,
treating the name as mere praise, heresy in gathering names, preaching Hari's name to the lazy and unbelievers,
forgetfulness of the name, and disrespect of the name — child, one should abandon from afar these very dreadful faults.
He should constantly think of Hari in the heart: "I am surrendered; he alone will always protect me."
I am yours, O lord of Radhika, in deed, mind and speech; and I am yours, O beloved of Krishna; you two alone are my refuge.
Servants, friends, parents and beloveds of Hari here are all eternal, O best of sages, to be thought of by the great-souled.
He goes to and from the forest and cow-pen daily, grazing cows with his comrades, and slaying demons —
the twelve friends of Hari are told, beginning with Shridama; Radhika's friends, Sushila and others, are said to be thirty-two.
Child, he should think of himself among them as a lovely girl, endowed with beauty and youth, well adorned,
skilled in various crafts and arts, suited to Krishna's pleasure, very content with the joy of delight in service to them.
From the Brahma-muhurta until midnight he should serve those two with fitting service at the proper times.
He should daily chant attentively the thousand names of the two. This practice has been told for the surrendered, O lord of sages.
It should not be told to anyone; I have revealed this truth to you. Sanatkumara said: "Then you, Narada, asked Sadashiva again,
and he told you the thousand names too; hear them from me. Having meditated in lovely Vrindavana, at the bank of the Yamuna,
taking refuge at the wish-tree, standing with Radhika, one should recite the thousand names called 'Yugala', O great sage.
Devakinandana, Shauri, Vasudeva, Baladeva's younger brother, Gadagraja, Kamsa's bewilderer, bewilderer of Kamsa's servants,
